root_cause.text: The old RX buffer pages were freed before the new allocation succeeded, so on failure the restore path reused freed page memory (use-after-free), and the new page pool leaked because it was overwritten without being destroyed.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `lan966x_fdma_rx_free_pages()` after successful allocation (lines removed from before the allocation and added to the success path), and adds saving of the old page array before allocation so that old pages are freed only on success. On the failure path, the old descriptors are restored with pages that were already freed, enabling DMA into freed memory. Additionally, the new `page_pool` pointer is overwritten without being destroyed on the restore path. The commit message explicitly states these issues.
